I love walleye, they are tied with trout as my favourite fish, and they are literally everywhere around me.

Walleye can be a tricky fish sometimes, the water temperature isn't really a factor, they are voracious predators and will feed daily winter or summer the trick to them is more in when(time of day) and where to fish for them.

Walleye really only feed twice a day, morning when the sun is coming up and evening when the sun is starting to fall, they will bite all day though if you can find where they are hiding and use a reaction type bait, something that wobbles or rattles or just stands out in some way.

For jigs/bait, Sometimes I use a sinker, hook and a minnow or a leech, #8 octopus hook I think usually but anything will do fine, or a jighead somewhere around 1/8th ounce, I like white and chartreuse but I don't think it matters. For the plastics themselves I like the berkley gulp, natural coloured shiners I think they are, and the leeches walleye love leeches. I think Gulp works just as good as live bait if not better.

Location is important, walleye like a few things, structure, oxygen, and escape to deep water.

Structure walleye like are places like points, dropoffs, weedbeds, rocks, creek/river mouths, If it's daytime and bright you want to fish as deep as possible, walleye hate brightness they have light sensitive eyes.

Summer fall and winter fish for them the same way in the same places, in the spring they move shallow to spawn and hang out shallow post spawn, so in the spring fish creek/river mouths, shallow sandy bays, shallow rocky areas etc...
